struct Gui.BreadcrumbCtrl[src]

A horizontal breadcrumb / path bar. Each level is drawn as "[icon] name >". Clicking a level body navigates to it (sigItemPressed); clicking its chevron opens a drop-down that the app fills with the level's children (sigFillMenu) and reports the chosen entry id (sigMenuSelected). The control is data-only: it knows nothing about what the levels mean, so it works for folders, categories, or any other hierarchy.

struct Gui.BreadcrumbItem[src]

One level of the path shown by a BreadcrumbCtrl (e.g. a folder). The app fills name/icon/userData; the rectangles are computed by the control's layout and used for hit-testing. hasArrow controls whether the level shows a drop-down chevron (the chevron of a level lists that level's children, the level to its right being the currently selected one).

struct Gui.FileBrowserCtrl[src]

A reusable file-browsing composite control: a shortcut/drive tree, a file list, a path combo and a name/type row. It is a plain window that can be embedded anywhere (a dialog, a side panel, a tab...) independently of FileDlg. FileDlg is just a thin modal wrapper around this control.

Reuses the public option types declared by FileDlg (FileDlgOptions/Mode/State) so existing callers keep working; the dialog-only fields (title, btnOkName) are simply ignored here.

struct Gui.ActionProperties[src]

The property grid's built-in context-menu commands, exposed through the shared gui action system (IActionUI) rather than a hardcoded addItem+doModal+switch(result). Registered on every Properties control in create(); the context menu (properties.menu.swg) just declares item ids, and doModal dispatches update()/execute() here. The target row is read from Properties.menuItem, so the very same commands could also be driven by a toolbar button or a keyboard shortcut (same WndId).

struct ActionProperties

struct Gui.PropFieldValue[src]

A captured copy of one field's value across every edited instance. Strings are copied by content (they own a heap buffer); every other supported type is copied as raw bytes. The per-instance addresses are captured too, so a value can be restored without the row it was recorded against: undo commands stay valid across a grid rebuild (clearStructs + addStruct), as long as the edited instances themselves are still alive.

struct PropFieldValue

Fields

NameTypeDescription
addrsCore.Array'(#null *u8)

field address in each captured instance

bytesCore.Array'(u8)

n * sz contiguous raw bytes (raw-bytes case)

isStringbool
nu64

number of instances captured

stringsCore.Array'(Core.String)

n strings (String case)

szu64

per-instance byte size (raw-bytes case only)

validbool

Methods

NameDescription
canSnapshot

True for the types the grid can snapshot/restore safely: dynamic String (by content) or

capture

Snapshot the current value of item across all its edited instances. Leaves the value

isEqual

Value equality (used to skip recording a no-op change).

restore

Write the captured value back into every captured instance address. Self-contained on
struct Gui.PropUndoCommand[src]

One undoable property edit: restore the old/new value at the instance addresses it was captured on. The command does not reference the row it came from: generation records the grid content it was built against, so a command replayed after a rebuild silently skips the row refresh (the values still land at the right addresses).

struct PropUndoCommand

interface Gui.IPropertyEditor[src]

A pluggable property editor. Register an implementing type with Properties.registerEditor (typically from a #init block); for each field the grid asks every registered editor whether it handles the field's type via canEdit, then builds the row via construct. This mirrors the image codec architecture (IImageDecoder / IImageEncoder): an interface + a type registry + per-use instantiation.

It is non-intrusive: the edited type is never touched. It lets ANY type (including primitives, enums, the built-in Color/vector types, or types you do not own) get a bespoke editor, registered from the outside. Because canEdit receives the type, one editor can claim a whole FAMILY of types (every enum, every type carrying a given attribute, a set of related structs), not just a single one — something a type-keyed map cannot express.

interface IPropertyEditor

Methods

NameDescription
canEdit

Return true if this editor should handle a field of type type.

construct

Build the editor row(s) for value (the field at data) under parent and return the

func Surface.setTrayIcon[src]

Show icon for this surface in the notification area (system tray), with an optional tooltip. Mouse interactions are delivered to the surface as WM_USER SysUserEvents whose param1 holds the raw mouse message (e.g. WM_RBUTTONDOWN for a right-click); handle them in the surface view's onSysUserEvent. The icon is removed automatically when the surface is destroyed.

This uses the legacy (version 0) NOTIFYICON behaviour on purpose: the callback carries the mouse message directly in lParam, which is what the window proc forwards as param1. NIM_SETVERSION/NOTIFYICON_VERSION_4 would change that layout and is intentionally not used.

mtd setTrayIcon(icon: Pixel.Image, tip: #null string = null)

func UndoManager.pushCmd[src]

Push a command onto the timeline. Any redo tail is discarded first (its commands are freed). serial groups this command with the others sharing the same value (0 = its own fresh group). When apply is true the command's redo() is invoked right away to make the change effective; pass false when the caller has already applied it.

Return true if this editor should handle a field of type type.

func IPropertyEditor.construct[src]

Build the editor row(s) for value (the field at data) under parent and return the created item — exactly like the built-in construct* methods. The recipe: call list.addItem(value, data, parent), create the editor widget(s) under item.line, wire their change callbacks to list.hasChanged(item), and add an item.sigRefresh handler that pushes the current value back into the widget(s). See values/color.swg and values/vector.swg.

An editor is a stateless singleton: it is invoked on a null instance (like canEdit), so me carries no per-field state — read any per-field configuration from value (its attributes), and wire data/item/list into the widget callbacks.

mtd construct(list: *Properties, value: Swag.TypeValue, data: #null [*] u8, parent: #null *PropertiesItem)->*PropertiesItem
func IPropertyNotify.fillPopupMenu[src]

Called when the user right-clicks a row: add custom menu items (each with a unique command id) before the built-in ones (Copy/Paste/...). Use a separator to set them apart.

mtd fillPopupMenu(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem, menu: *MenuCtrl)
func IPropertyNotify.isEnumValueVisible[src]

Return false to hide one value of an enum field (a value that makes no sense for the host, e.g. a None entry): the combo omits it, an enum-flags block skips its row. Like isItemVisible, checked on the host notify and along the item's parent chain, but when the row is BUILT: rebuild the grid content to re-evaluate it.

mtd isEnumValueVisible(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem, enumValue: Swag.TypeValue)->bool
func IPropertyNotify.isItemAtDefault[src]

Customize the "is this field still at its default value?" test, used to decide whether the row shows the revert marker. Return .Auto (the default) to let the grid compare the current value against the value the field is initialized to in the struct declaration; return .AtDefault / .Modified to force the answer when the test is more involved than a plain comparison. The first non-Auto result along the item's parent chain wins.

mtd isItemAtDefault(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem)->PropDefaultState
func IPropertyNotify.isItemEnabled[src]
mtd isItemEnabled(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem)->bool
func IPropertyNotify.isItemReadOnly[src]

Return true to make item read-only at runtime: shown but not editable, and "Paste" is disabled. Unlike isItemEnabled (which grays the whole row), this only locks the editor. The static equivalent is the Properties.ReadOnly attribute. Checked along the parent chain.

mtd isItemReadOnly(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem)->bool
func IPropertyNotify.isItemVisible[src]
mtd isItemVisible(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem)->bool
func IPropertyNotify.itemHasChanged[src]

item is null when the change is not tied to a live row anymore: an undo/redo restore recorded against a previous grid content (the values are already back in the instances).

mtd itemHasChanged(list: *Properties, item: #null *PropertiesItem)
func IPropertyNotify.onPopupCommand[src]

Called with the command id chosen in the popup menu when it is not one of the built-in actions. Return true once handled. This is how custom fillPopupMenu items are executed.

mtd onPopupCommand(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem, cmdId: string)->bool
func IPropertyNotify.resetItemToDefault[src]

Reset item to its default value yourself; return true once handled. Return false (the default) to let the grid restore the value declared in the struct. Called by the "Reset to default" action and the revert marker. Checked along the item's parent chain.

mtd resetItemToDefault(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem)->bool
func IPropertyNotify.validateItem[src]

Return a validation state + message for item. Called on build and after every change; the row shows an accent bar + badge in the state color and the message as a tooltip. The most severe result along the item's parent chain wins.

mtd validateItem(list: *Properties, item: *PropertiesItem)->PropValidationResult

Create a row for value (field typeinfo + name) bound to data under parentItem. Public so custom editors registered with registerEditor (possibly authored in another module) can build their row the same way the built-in editors do.

mtd addItem(value: Swag.TypeValue, data: #null *u8, parentItem: #null *PropertiesItem, height: f32 = 0, flags = AddItemFlags.Name | AddItemFlags.Description)->*PropertiesItem

A thin horizontal separator row, the same look as a Panel category divider. Public so a host appending hand-made rows (addItem) after the generated content can separate them; call endAppendRows once done. name feeds the notify visibility dispatch and the filter.

mtd addSeparator(name: #null string = null, parentItem: #null *PropertiesItem = null)->*PropertiesItem
func Properties.addStruct[src]

func Properties.addStructMulti[src]

Add several instances of the SAME struct type for multi-selection editing. bases holds the base address of each instance to edit together (>= 1). Editing a field writes it into every instance; a field whose value differs across the instances is shown as "mixed". With a single base this behaves like addStruct. With onlyNamed, only the fields carrying an explicit Properties.Name attribute get a row: the grid becomes opt-in, for structs whose fields are mostly internal state.

mtd addStructMulti(typeof: typeinfo, bases: [..] *u8, section: #null string = null, onlyNamed = false)
func Properties.assignInstances[src]

Fill in the per-instance field addresses of every item created since fromIdx. Each field sits at a fixed offset from its struct base, so its address in instance k is base[k] + (item.data - base[0]). Items under a dynamic array keep a single address (their element storage is not at a fixed struct offset).

mtd assignInstances(fromIdx: u64, bases: [..] *u8)

Returns a unique file path in a dedicated swag-tests sub-folder of the system temp folder (created on demand). func HeadlessHost.bindApplication[src]

Binds another Application instance to this host: the code under test may read its own module-global Application (theme, renderer, options) while events flow through the host. The renderer goes headless and the host's theme and style are shared instead of being rebuilt.

func HeadlessHost.clickModalButtonWhenShown[src]

Arms the auto UI driver to click button in the topmost modal surface as soon as it exists. Modal loops pump sigFrame every frame, so this drives dialogs opened by the code under test without any test-side closure. If the expected UI never shows up within maxFrames frames, the pending loop is cancelled and autoHandled stays false.

func RadioButton.uncheckGroupSiblings[src]

Uncheck the sibling radios that share this one's (parent, group). No-op when this radio's group is empty, so opting out keeps the old "grouping is the caller's job" behavior (and two ungrouped radios never match each other). Recursion is bounded: it only unchecks, and setChecked(false) never re-enters this.

mtd uncheckGroupSiblings()
